stem: An overweight adolescent boy is worried that his penis looks small; what is the most appropriate approach during pubertal assessment?

options.text: Assume micropenis based on appearance alone
Ignore pubertal staging because body habitus explains everything
Consider a buried penis in boys with high BMI and perform formal pubertal assessment
Use penile appearance alone instead of assessing testicular volume
Conclude the appearance must reflect torsion-related change

explanation: Formal pubertal assessment is the best approach. Consider a buried penis in boys with high BMI and assess puberty properly, including testicular volume rather than relying on appearance alone.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

rationale: High BMI can make penile appearance misleading during puberty assessment, so a buried penis should be considered and pubertal staging should still be performed.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because micropenis should not be assumed from appearance alone, particularly when a buried penis may be present.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because body habitus does not replace formal pubertal assessment.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because a buried penis can be a pitfall in boys with high BMI, and formal pubertal assessment should still be performed.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because penile appearance alone is not enough; testicular volume is part of proper pubertal assessment.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because torsion is not the relevant explanation for this presentation.
